items.quote: And Moses besought the LORD his God, and said, LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people
items.claim: The text says Moses pleaded with God and asked why God's anger burned against the people.

items.quote: which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand
items.claim: Moses' plea says God brought the people out of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand.
items.mechanism: great power, and with a mighty hand

items.quote: Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains, and to consume them from the face of the earth?
items.claim: Moses argues that destroying the people would let the Egyptians say God freed them only to kill them. This is an appeal to God's reputation.

items.quote: Turn from thy fierce wrath, and repent of this evil against thy people.
items.claim: Moses asks God to turn away from his anger and to reconsider ("repent of") the harm he planned against the people.

items.quote: 32:11 And Moses besought the LORD his God
items.claim: Unverified model-prior: the verse numbers and wording suggest this is Exodus 32:11-12 in the King James Version, during the golden calf episode. The document itself does not name the book, translation or context.
